st: In season 1, the Bus carries Coulson's team on its missions.
In season 1, Ward steals the Bus for HYDRA, and Garrett's people keep it at a base in Havana.
In season 2, Coulson's team flies the Bus again for the rebuilt S.H.I.E.L.D.
In season 2, HYDRA missiles shoot it down on the way to an Arctic base.
In season 1, Coulson's beloved Corvette rides in the Bus's hold, and it turns out it can fly.
In season 7, Mack gives the new Coulson a restored Lola, and he drives off in it to travel the world.

k: A non-lethal stun gun made by Fitz and Simmons
st: In season 1, Fitz and Simmons build a stun gun, and Ward uses it to drop Mike Peterson without killing him.

k: A Tesseract-powered HYDRA weapon found in Peru
st: In season 1, the team takes a Tesseract-powered HYDRA weapon from Peru, and S.H.I.E.L.D. locks it in the Fridge.
In season 1, Ward and Garrett raid the Fridge and steal it for HYDRA.
In season 1, Coulson turns it on the rebuilt Garrett at Cybertek and destroys him.

k: A salvaged helmet carrying an alien virus
st: In season 1, a Chitauri helmet from New York spreads a deadly virus that nearly kills Simmons, then goes to Agent Blake.

k: An Asgardian staff that fills its holder with rage
st: In season 1, the team gathers the staff's three pieces and uses it against a pagan hate group, then stores it in the Fridge.
In season 1, Ward and Garrett raid the Fridge and steal it for HYDRA.
In season 1, May takes it from a HYDRA agent in Cuba and uses it to bring the base down.

k: An Asgardian collar that silences Lorelei
st: In season 1, Sif locks the collar on Lorelei to end her mind control and takes her back to Asgard.

k: A rare element that controls gravity
st: In season 1, Ian Quinn builds a gravitonium generator, and Franklin Hall is swallowed by the gravitonium.
In season 1, S.H.I.E.L.D. locks the gravitonium away in the Fridge.
In season 1, Garrett steals it from the Fridge, and Quinn and Raina flee Cybertek with it.
In season 5, the team finds the lost Cybertek ship Principia, and Mack collects the gravitonium left aboard.
In season 5, Talbot climbs into the infusion chamber at the Lighthouse and absorbs the remaining gravitonium.
In season 5, Talbot grows too powerful to stop, until Daisy blasts him into space.

k: The drug that brought Coulson back to life
st: In season 1, Fitz finds the drug that revived Coulson and uses it to save Skye; it comes from a blue alien body.
In season 2, the drug drives Coulson to carve alien symbols, which turn out to map a hidden Kree city.
In season 5, the Ghost Rider spirit has burned the drug out of Coulson's body, and he is dying.

k: A super soldier serum built on Extremis
st: In season 1, Project Centipede's Extremis-based serum powers Mike Peterson, Centipede's soldiers and finally Garrett.
In season 5, Tony Caine gives Daisy the last of the serum that once kept Garrett alive.
In season 5, the dying Coulson refuses it and hides it in Daisy's gauntlets, and she injects it to stop Talbot.

k: A box of S.H.I.E.L.D. secrets left by Fury
st: In season 1, Nick Fury brings his toolbox of S.H.I.E.L.D. secrets to Coulson.
In season 1, Fury names Coulson director and hands him the toolbox, which leads him to a secret base.
In season 2, Bobbi Morse steals it from Coulson's office for Gonzales's S.H.I.E.L.D.
In season 2, Fitz slips away with it and opens it to reach Coulson.

k: A Kree key that HYDRA calls the Obelisk
st: In season 2, in 1945, Peggy Carter's SSR seizes the Obelisk from the last known HYDRA base.
In season 2, Carl Creel steals it in the present for HYDRA, but it ends up with Raina and Skye's father.
In season 2, Skye's father delivers the Obelisk to Whitehall himself.
In season 2, Raina takes it into the Kree temple, where it opens, kills Trip and transforms Skye and Raina.

k: Kree crystals whose mist awakens Inhumans
st: In season 2, the Diviner's Terrigen transforms Skye, and Jiaying's Afterlife keeps crystals to transform its people.
In season 2, Jiaying tries to spread crystals from a Quinjet, but Skye pushes the plane into the ocean.
In season 3, Terrigen from the sea spreads around the world in fish oil, and Hive uses it to give James powers.
In season 4, Radcliffe hands Terrigen to the Superior, and it turns the Watchdog Tucker Shockley into an Inhuman.
In season 5, the Kree on the Lighthouse force young people through Terrigenesis to breed Inhumans.

k: A Kree stone that swallows people whole
st: In season 2, the Monolith sits in the Iliad's cargo hold, and at season's end it swallows Simmons.
In season 3, Fitz learns it is a portal and brings Simmons back from an alien planet just as Daisy shatters it.
In season 5, a monolith sends the team to 2091 and back; later a bomb shatters three monoliths, and Fitz seals their rift.
In season 6, Izel takes the monoliths' trapped energy and makes Flint rebuild them, but the Chronicoms destroy them.

k: A HYDRA mask that copies another person's face
st: In season 2, HYDRA's Agent 33 wears May's face with it; once repaired, it lets her become anyone, and she frees Bakshi.
In season 2, Ward accidentally kills Agent 33 while she wears May's face.

k: A HYDRA machine that digs into memories
st: In season 2, Coulson uses HYDRA's memory machine to find other patients of the T.A.H.I.T.I. program.

k: One of Fury's old helicarriers, rebuilt in secret
st: In season 2, Coulson's agents secretly refit one of Fury's old helicarriers under the Theta Protocol.
In season 2, Fury flies it to Sokovia to save its people.
In season 2, the carrier is home to Gonzales's S.H.I.E.L.D., until Jiaying's Inhumans briefly seize it to spread Terrigen.
In season 3, Zephyr One becomes S.H.I.E.L.D.'s command plane, until Hive steals it to launch his warhead.
In season 3, May and Fitz get aboard and free Daisy, and the team takes the plane back.
In season 4, the Zephyr guards Daisy and Simmons while they are in the Framework, then carries the team on the run.
In season 5, the Zephyr sits with the team's old tech in General Hale's military facility.
In season 5, Fitz steals it back, and it later carries the team into space on gravitonium power.
In season 6, Sarge seizes the Zephyr from Mack on the way to the Shrike tower.
In season 6, Simmons arrives in an upgraded Zephyr to rescue the team.
In season 7, the Zephyr jumps through time after the Chronicoms, until Nathaniel Malick takes it into space.
In season 7, the team wins the Zephyr back and escapes the Chronicoms' ship in it.

k: A record of Inhumans kept by Daisy's mother
st: In season 3, Andrew Garner opens the ledger, and its Terrigen trap turns him into Lash, who uses it to hunt Inhumans.

k: The artificial hand that replaces Coulson's own
st: In season 3, Coulson wears a prosthetic hand after losing his own, and uses it to kill Ward on Maveth.

k: An ancient device that summons the Kree
st: In season 3, J.T. James, an Inhuman who knows about Hive, keeps an ancient Kree device.
In season 3, James gives the device to Daisy and Lincoln.
In season 3, Hive later activates it and calls two Kree Reapers to Earth.

k: A stolen warhead loaded with a pathogen
st: In season 3, Hive's followers steal a warhead from the ATCU, and Hive loads it with Radcliffe's pathogen.
In season 3, Lincoln flies it into space in a Quinjet, where it explodes.

k: An ancient book of dark knowledge
st: In season 4, scientists at Momentum Labs study the Darkhold, and Joseph Bauer hides it after their experiment goes wrong.
In season 4, May takes the book and hides it for S.H.I.E.L.D.
In season 4, May gives it to Radcliffe to save Coulson, and his android Aida reads it.
In season 4, Aida tries to take it, but Mack stops her, and Coulson has the book hidden in the Koenigs' Labyrinth.
In season 4, Radcliffe steals it for the Superior, Anton Ivanov.
In season 4, S.H.I.E.L.D. takes it back from Ivanov, and Ghost Rider carries it through a portal.

k: A muscle car that burns with hellfire
st: In season 4, Robbie Reyes drives his uncle's Dodge Charger, and as Ghost Rider he sets it ablaze.

k: A secret serum behind Director Mace's strength
st: In season 4, a secret government serum gives Director Mace his powers, though each dose he takes risks killing him.

k: A virtual world built by Radcliffe and Aida
st: In season 4, Aida traps the agents in Radcliffe's virtual world, the Framework, where HYDRA rules.
In season 4, Aida shuts the Framework down once she has a human body.

k: A cryogenic pod that carries Fitz into the future
st: In season 5, Fitz steals a cryo pod from Hale's base and sleeps in it on Enoch's ship for 74 years to reach the team.
In season 6, Daisy and Simmons find Enoch's ship abandoned in space and the cryo pod empty.

k: A Kree drug that drives people to violence
st: In season 5, Kasius drives fighters mad with odium and finally takes it himself.
In season 5, back on Earth, Simmons studies the odium, until May destroys the last vial.
In season 5, the Cybertek ship Principia goes missing with gravitonium aboard, which lifts it into the sky.
In season 5, the team finds it floating and takes the gravitonium left aboard before it crashes.

k: A HYDRA machine that fuses a person with gravitonium
st: In season 5, Hale's HYDRA infuses Ruby with gravitonium in Whitehall's particle-infusion chamber.
In season 5, the chamber ends up in S.H.I.E.L.D.'s Lighthouse, where Talbot climbs in and absorbs the gravitonium.

k: Crystal blades that kill the Shrike
st: In season 6, Sarge's crew kills Shrike hosts with crystal knives.
In season 6, Yo-Yo recovers a knife, and Deke's team turns the crystal into Shrike-killing bullets.

k: The drive that lets the Zephyr jump through time
st: In season 6, Fitz uses an upgraded jump drive to send the Zephyr and the team decades into the past.
In season 7, the time drive follows the Chronicoms through history until it nearly fails, and Enoch gives his life to fix it.
In season 7, the Chronicoms plan to blow up Area 51 with Helius in 1955, but Daisy and Simmons shut it down with an EMP.

k: Project Insight, launched decades too early
st: In season 7, in 1973, S.H.I.E.L.D. under Wilfred Malick prepares Project Insight decades ahead of time.
In season 7, Insight launches in 1976, and the agents use the Zephyr to destroy it.

k: The Chronicoms' window onto the future
st: In season 7, the time stream that Sibyl uses to predict the future is kept at S.H.I.E.L.D.'s Lighthouse.
In season 7, Sibyl's hunter robots raid the Lighthouse, and a small robot carries it off to Nathaniel Malick.

k: A weapon Victor Ramon tries to sell
st: Holding Elena captive, Victor Ramon tries to sell a weapon to the Watchdogs.
Quake comes for the weapon, and it vaporizes Ramon as S.H.I.E.L.D. arrives.
Elena steals Director Mace's access card to dig up information on Victor Ramon.
May catches on, and Elena reluctantly hands the card back to her.
In season 1, Leviathan turns Howard's stolen nitramene formula into bombs at a Roxxon refinery.
In season 1, one bomb destroys the refinery, and the rest implode with the truck carrying them.
In season 3, the Watchdogs attack an ATCU facility with nitramene bombs, a weapon Howard Stark once created.

k: Dangerous weapons stolen from Howard's vault
st: In season 1, Leviathan smuggles Howard's inventions out of his vault and onto a ship.
In season 1, Peggy tracks them to the ship, and the SSR seizes them.

k: A typewriter that receives Leviathan's coded orders
st: In season 1, the SSR finds the typewriter in Demidov's hotel room, and Peggy decodes a Leviathan message sent through it.

k: The last vial of Captain America's blood
st: In season 1, Howard Stark hides a vial of Steve's blood inside a device he calls the Blitzkrieg Button.
In season 1, Peggy finds the vial, keeps it secret, and finally pours it into the East River.

k: Howard's gas that drives people to kill
st: In season 1, Fennhoff has Dooley steal a cylinder from the SSR, and he and Dottie gas a cinema with Midnight Oil.
In season 1, Fennhoff hypnotizes Howard to drop the gas on Times Square, but Peggy talks him down.

k: One of Howard's inventions, rigged to explode
st: In season 1, a hypnotized Dooley wears an experimental vest of Howard's, given to him by Fennhoff.
In season 1, it cannot be shut off, so Dooley leaps from a window before it explodes.

k: A dark substance found by Isodyne Energy
st: In season 2, Whitney Frost absorbs Zero Matter at Isodyne Energy and takes more from Jane Scott's body.
In season 2, Wilkes uses Zero Matter taken from Frost to restore his body, and a rift fills him with more.
In season 2, Wilkes unleashes all of his Zero Matter, and Frost absorbs it.
In season 2, a gamma cannon drives the Zero Matter out of her and into another dimension.

k: Howard's cannon for closing Zero Matter rifts
st: In season 2, Howard's gamma cannon closes a Zero Matter rift, and later blasts the Zero Matter out of Whitney Frost.

k: A secret key of the Council of Nine
st: In season 2, Thompson finds a secret Council of Nine key among Masters's things.
In season 2, Thompson gives the key to Peggy.

k: A file meant to incriminate Peggy Carter
st: In season 2, Thompson finds Masters's file on Peggy.
In season 2, a gunman shoots Thompson in his hotel room and takes the file.

k: A vibranium shield made by Howard Stark
st: In season 1, Howard Stark secretly gives Peggy a vibranium shield, and she fights HYDRA with it as Captain Carter.

k: A Tesseract-powered battle suit for Steve Rogers
st: In season 1, Howard builds the Hydra Stomper for Steve with Tesseract power, and Steve pilots it against HYDRA.
In season 1, decades later, Carter and Natasha find the armor with someone inside.
In season 2, Steve, trapped in the suit and brainwashed by the Red Room, attacks Carter and Natasha.
In season 2, Carter breaks through to Steve, and he blows up the suit to destroy the Red Room.
In season 1, Carter takes the Tesseract from HYDRA, and Howard uses it to power the Hydra Stomper.
In season 1, the Red Skull uses it at a HYDRA base to open a portal and summon a monster.
In season 1, almost 70 years later, it opens another portal, and Carter steps out to meet Fury and Clint.

k: Cosmic dust that can end hunger
st: In season 1, the Embers of Genesis sit in Taneleer Tivan's collection on Knowhere.
In season 1, Nebula and Star-Lord T'Challa's Ravagers steal the Embers.

n: The Eye of Agamotto (Strange Supreme's world)
k: A relic that can turn back time
st: In season 1, Strange finds the Eye of Agamotto at Kamar-Taj, and the Ancient One warns him not to misuse it.
In season 1, Strange uses the Eye again and again to save Christine, but she dies in every timeline.

k: A virus from the Quantum Realm that makes zombies
st: In season 1, Janet infects Hank Pym with a virus from the Quantum Realm, and it turns most of Earth into zombies.
Five years on, Wanda rules the zombies as their queen and infects New Asgard by feeding it zombie flesh.

k: The six Infinity Stones of the zombie world
st: In season 1, Vision uses the Mind Stone to try to reverse the zombie virus.
In season 1, Vision gives Peter Parker the Mind Stone; in Wakanda, a zombie Thanos waits with a nearly full Gauntlet.
In a flashback, the zombie Thanos rules Wakanda and tries to snap the Infinity Gauntlet.
T'Challa pushes zombie Thanos into Wakanda's vibranium core, destroying the stones; Bruce Banner absorbs their energy.
Wanda takes the stones' energy from the Infinity Hulk and persuades Kamala to help her remake the world.

k: Combat drones built by Tony Stark and Killmonger
st: In season 1, Tony and Killmonger build combat drones out of vibranium.
In season 1, after Tony's death, Ross sends the drone army against Wakanda, where it is defeated.

k: The six stones Ultron uses to end all life
st: In season 1, Ultron takes the Mind Stone and then the rest from Thanos, and wipes out life in his universe.
In season 1, Killmonger grabs for the stones, and Strange Supreme seals them away with him.
In season 2, Killmonger fights in armor powered by the stones.
In season 2, Kahhori pulls Killmonger out of his armor, and Captain Carter turns the stones on Strange Supreme.

k: Gamora's device for destroying Infinity Stones
st: In season 1, Gamora brings the Crusher to destroy Ultron's stones, but it fails because they come from another universe.
In season 2, Ronan's ship, the Dark Aster, comes for Xandar after his coup against Thanos.
In season 2, Nebula's altered code closes Xandar's shield as the Dark Aster enters, destroying it and killing Ronan.

k: A seed of Ego's living power
st: In season 2, Ego overwhelms Peggy Carter's team as he tries to obtain his seed on Earth.
In season 2, Peter Quill gets to the seed first and uses it to destroy Ego's avatar.

k: A sample of the Hulk's blood
st: In season 2, Avengers Tower holds a sample of Bruce Banner's blood, and Justin Hammer raids the Tower for it.
In season 2, trying to secure it, Happy Hogan is injected with it and becomes the Freak.

k: An Iron Man suit Tony builds on Sakaar
st: In season 2, the stranded Tony builds a new Iron Man suit on Sakaar and wins the Grandmaster's race.

k: A cube that fell into a Mohawk lake
st: In season 2, the Tesseract falls into a lake after Asgard's fall, and the lake sends Kahhori to the Sky World, giving her powers.
In season 2, Odin enchants Hela's crown against the unworthy; she earns it back by fighting beside Wenwu against Odin.

k: A scepter holding the Time Stone
st: In season 2, King Thor holds the Time Stone in his scepter.
In season 2, Carter and Rogers's outlaws steal it from Thor's court to power Tony Stark's device.

k: Strange Supreme's machine to rebuild his universe
st: In season 2, Strange Supreme feeds captured variants to the Forge to bring back his lost universe.
In season 2, the Forge collapses, and Strange sacrifices himself to it.

k: Giant mechs built to fight gamma monsters
st: In season 3, the Avengers build giant mechs to fight the Apex, but are killed.
In season 3, the new Avengers pilot the mechs and combine them with Banner's Mighty Avenger Protocol.

k: Super soldier serum taken from the Starks
st: In season 3, in 1991, Howard and Maria Stark have a case of super-soldier serum.
In season 3, Alexei and Bucky take one vial of the serum from the Starks.
In season 3, Alexei destroys the vial in Las Vegas.

k: Nanites that power Quentin Beck's illusions
st: In season 3, Quentin Beck's nanites power his illusions and drones, and he uploads them into himself.
In season 3, Riri Williams siphons the nanites out of Beck.
In season 3, shards of the Watchers' Observational Plane spill into the multiverse.
In season 3, Carter's team finds three shards and loses two trying to synthesize them.
In season 3, Infinity Ultron absorbs the last shard.
In season 3, Storm, the Goddess of Thunder, wields Mjolnir on Captain Carter's team against multiversal threats.

k: A shrunken transmitter for calling the Nova Corps
st: Kamala's group finds the transmitter inside a zombie Erik Selvig and activates it in space, reaching the Nova Corps.

k: Wenwu's rings, passed to his son
st: In a flashback, Wenwu's Ten Rings organization saves Shang-Chi's group from a zombie horde.
Wenwu gives his bitten son the rings to hold back the infection, and Shang-Chi fights the zombies with them.
Shang-Chi is killed by the zombie hordes in the battle for the Infinity Hulk.

k: A ship from New Asgard that can reach space
st: The survivors flee New Asgard in an Asgardian ship to reach space.
The Nova Corps shoot the ship down, and the sorcerers of Kamar-Taj rescue the group.

k: Thor's board of clues about the Infinity Stones
Team Thor, Team Thor: Part 2 & Team Darryl
st: Thor shows off his board tracking the Infinity Stones, the Avengers, Nick Fury and Thanos.
Team Thor, Team Thor: Part 2 & Team Darryl

k: The Grandmaster's weapon that melts people
Team Thor, Team Thor: Part 2 & Team Darryl
st: The Grandmaster, now Darryl's roommate, melts one of Darryl's friends when a video shoot lets him down.
Team Thor, Team Thor: Part 2 & Team Darryl
